title: Filtered projective model for filtered-origin endomorphisms
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, and call an object of the ordinary module derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] perfect when it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Let $DF_2(A)$ be the localization of the homotopy category of pairs of cochain complexes $K'\subset K$ at the filtration-preserving chain maps that induce quasi-isomorphisms on $K'$ and $K/K'$; homotopies are maps $h^i:K^i\to L^{i-1}$ with $f-g=dh+hd$ and $h^i(K'^i)\subseteq L'^{i-1}$. Thus the filtration is $0\subset K'\subset K$, with the two graded pieces defined by subcomplex and quotient [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Suppose $\mathcal P\in DF_2(A)$ has perfect graded pieces, and let $u:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P$ be any endomorphism in this localized category. Then there are bounded complexes $M'\subset M$ and $M''=M/M'$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules, an isomorphism $(M'\subset M)\cong\mathcal P$ in $DF_2(A)$, and a filtration-preserving chain endomorphism $\bar u$ of $(M'\subset M)$ whose localized image is $u$ under this isomorphism. The exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ splits in every cochain degree. The restricted and quotient chain endomorphisms represent the endomorphisms induced by $u$ on the two graded pieces. Here filtration-preserving means $\bar u(M')\subseteq M'$; it does not assert that $\bar u(F^iM)=\operatorname{im}(\bar u)\cap F^iM$.

external.place: Clause (2), paragraph beginning “an object of DF(A) with a two-step filtration and perfect graded pieces is represented by a filtered bounded complex of finite projective modules” and following representative assertion.

proof.text: Choose a representative $K'\subset K$ of $\mathcal P$, and write $K''=K/K'$. By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], choose bounded finite-projective representatives $P',P''$ of its two graded objects, and a common upper cohomology bound $N$ for $K',K''$. The same bound holds for $K$: if $z\in K^i$ is a cycle with $i>N$, its image in $K''$ is a boundary; lift a primitive, subtract its differential from $z$, and then write the remaining cycle in $K'$ as a boundary. Define $T^i=K^i$ for $i<N$, $T^N=\ker(d_K^N)$ and $T^i=0$ for $i>N$, and define $T'$ in the same way from $K'$. Thus $T'\subset T$ is bounded above as a complex. The inclusions $T'\to K'$ and $T\to K$ induce isomorphisms on cohomology. The quotient map $T/T'\to K''$ is also a quasi-isomorphism: in degrees below $N-1$ its cycle and boundary formulas coincide with those of $K''$; in degree $N-1$, if a lift has differential in $K'^N$, this differential is already a cycle, so the quotient cycle condition is unchanged; in degree $N$, a cycle in $K''$ lifts to $x\in K^N$ with $dx\in K'^{N+1}$, and $H^{N+1}(K')=0$ lets us subtract $y\in K'^N$ with $dy=dx$. A class in $T/T'$ mapping to a boundary has $x-dt\in K'^N$, which is a cycle and hence vanishes in $(T/T')^N$. Above $N$ both cohomologies vanish. Therefore $(T'\subset T)\to(K'\subset K)$ is a filtered quasi-isomorphism in precisely the unbounded two-step localization in the statement; no identification of cohomological boundedness with termwise boundedness is being used.

source.place: Tag 03TB (trace-lemma-filtered-derived-category), preceded by the explicit good-truncation cycle calculation needed to enter DF^-

proof.text: Apply the two-step replacement assertion of [lem-trf-filtered-projective-comparison] to the bounded-above pair $T'\subset T$. It gives a bounded-above two-step pair $Q'\subset Q$, with projective graded modules, and a filtered quasi-isomorphism to $T'\subset T$. Write $Q''=Q/Q'$. In each degree, lift the identity of the projective module $(Q'')^n$ along $Q^n\twoheadrightarrow(Q'')^n$ using [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. These degreewise splittings identify $Q^n=(Q')^n\oplus(Q'')^n$ and its differential with $\begin{pmatrix}d_{Q'}&\eta\\0&d_{Q''}\end{pmatrix}$. The equation $d_Q^2=0$ says $d_{Q'}\eta+\eta d_{Q''}=0$, so $\eta:Q''\to Q'[1]$ is a chain map under the shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This matrix description holds for bounded-above $Q$, with no finite-generation or lower-bound assumption. A different section, obtained by adding $s^n:(Q'')^n\to(Q')^n$, changes the off-diagonal map to $\eta+d_{Q'}s-sd_{Q''}$; this is the negative of the chain-homotopy boundary for maps into $Q'[1]$.

source.place: Tag 03TB (trace-lemma-filtered-derived-category); degreewise splitting and block calculation, with cone convention Tags 014E/014F in derived.tex

proof.text:
The chosen isomorphisms of graded derived objects give isomorphisms $a':P'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'$ and $a'':P''\xrightarrow{\sim}Q''$ in $D(A)$. The surjectivity in [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], applied to bounded projective sources $P'$ and $P''$ and unrestricted targets $Q',Q''$, gives chain representatives $\alpha',\alpha''$. They are quasi-isomorphisms since their derived images are isomorphisms and cohomology factors through the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Form $\delta=(a'[1])^{-1}\eta a'':P''\to P'[1]$ in $D(A)$. The same surjectivity gives a chain map $\xi:P''\to P'[1]$ representing $\delta$. The two chain maps $\alpha'[1]\xi$ and $\eta\alpha''$ from the bounded projective source $P''$ to $Q'[1]$ now have equal images in $D(A)$. The injectivity in the same representative bijection gives a chain homotopy. Taking its negative, write its degree components as $h^n:(P'')^n\to(Q')^n$ so that
$\alpha'^{n+1}\xi^n-\eta^n\alpha''^n=d_{Q'}^nh^n-h^{n+1}d_{P''}^n$.
The minus sign here is forced by $d_{Q'[1]}=-d_{Q'}$.

source.place: Tags 014E (derived-definition-cone) and 014F (derived-lemma-functorial-cone); ordinary derived-map bijection supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Define $M'=P'$, $M^n=(P')^n\oplus(P'')^n$, and $d_M^n=\begin{pmatrix}d_{P'}^n&\xi^n\\0&d_{P''}^n\end{pmatrix}$, with $M'$ the first summand. Because $\xi$ maps into $P'[1]$, its chain-map equation is $d_{P'}\xi+\xi d_{P''}=0$; multiplication of the differential matrix therefore gives $d_M^2=0$. Coordinate inclusion and projection identify $M/M'=P''$ and split $0\to M'\to M\to P''\to0$ in every degree. Finite generating sets for the two summands generate $M^n$, and two maps from projective summands lift separately along a surjection, so the terms of $M$ are finitely generated projective [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module]; the union of the two finite degree ranges bounds $M$. Define $B^n=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha'^n&h^n\\0&\alpha''^n\end{pmatrix}:M^n\to Q^n$. The top-right chain-map equality $d_{Q'}^nh^n+\eta^n\alpha''^n=\alpha'^{n+1}\xi^n+h^{n+1}d_{P''}^n$ is exactly the identity proved in step 3; the diagonal equalities hold because $\alpha',\alpha''$ are chain maps. Thus $B$ is filtration-preserving, and its graded maps are the quasi-isomorphisms $\alpha',\alpha''$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. It is a filtered quasi-isomorphism, so the zigzag $M\xrightarrow{B}Q\to T\to K$, with all subcomplexes retained, gives the required isomorphism in $DF_2(A)$. This proves the filtered isomorphism directly, without classifying objects by their triangles.

source.place: Tags 014E (derived-definition-cone) and 014F (derived-lemma-functorial-cone), explicit block differential and homotopy-square matrix

proof.text: Let $j:(M'\subset M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal P$ be the isomorphism of step 4. The two-step, unrestricted-target bijection in [lem-trf-filtered-projective-comparison] applies to $M$ because it is bounded above and its two graded modules are projective in every degree. It therefore represents $j^{-1}uj$ by a filtration-preserving chain map $\bar u:(M'\subset M)\to(M'\subset M)$. The same node also identifies this Hom set with the Hom set in the globally finite filtered localization when both pairs are embedded with $F^0=M$, $F^1=M'$ and $F^2=0$. This compatibility is additional to the comparison inside $DF_2(A)$ needed for the item. This step uses the comparison in unbounded $DF_2(A)$, not merely Tag 03TB's bounded-above localization.

source.place: Tag 03TJ (trace-section-filtrations-perfect), full faithfulness in DF; the strengthened comparison node states the two-step unrestricted-localization assertion

proof.text: Filtration preservation gives $\bar u(M')\subseteq M'$. Restricting the chain-map equation yields a chain endomorphism of $M'$, and taking its quotient yields one of $M/M'$. The subcomplex and quotient operations [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] preserve homotopies of the stipulated kind and send filtered quasi-isomorphisms to ordinary quasi-isomorphisms. They therefore factor through the localization; applied to $j^{-1}uj$, these two operations show that the restricted and quotient endomorphisms represent exactly the graded endomorphisms induced by $u$. This is filtration preservation and makes no assertion about intersection with the image.

source.place: Tag 0121 (homology-definition-filtered), filtered morphisms; Tag 012K (homology-section-filtered-complex, definition-filtered-complex), subcomplex and quotient; the factorization follows directly from the localization universal property.
